# CG-RES-025: Response body removed

A response no longer has a body.

**Why it matters:** Consumers parse documented bodies.

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| Area | [Responses](./#res) |
| Detects | `response.bodyRemoved` |
| Severity | breaking: high · potentially breaking: medium · undetermined: medium |
| Classification can be overridden | no (the rule only fires when the change is breaking by definition) |

## Message

> The body of {where} was removed.
>
> Consumers that parse the body will receive none.
>
> **Fix:** Keep the body, or release as a new major version.

## Examples

Each example is an executed test case of the rule (`packages/engine/test/compat/fixtures.ts`).

### Fires: body removed

```diff
  openapi: 3.1.0
  info: {title: t, version: v}
  paths:
    /x:
      get:
-       responses: {'200': {description: ok, content: {application/json: {}}}}
+       responses: {'200': {description: ok}}
```

**Result:** Breaking, high. The body of GET /x: response 200 was removed.

### Does not fire: one of two media types removed

```diff
  openapi: 3.1.0
  info: {title: t, version: v}
  paths:
    /x:
      get:
-       responses: {'200': {description: ok, content: {application/json: {}, application/xml: {}}}}
+       responses: {'200': {description: ok, content: {application/json: {}}}}
```

**Result:** no finding from this rule.

## Silence or tune it

```yaml
rules:
  ignore:
    - rule: CG-RES-025
      operation: "GET /example"   # optional: narrow it down
      reason: "Explain why this is acceptable"
      expires: 2027-01-01         # optional
  overrides:
    CG-RES-025: { severity: low }
```
